user: Do NOT recommend any mountainside properties, because we want to walk to restaurants in Gion in the evenings instead of taking taxis back. Which Kyoto districts are best for evening strolls, and are any particularly lively in April?
text:
The Gion district, southwest of Kawaramachi, is the most compact for evening strolling. You'll walk past machiya townhouses converted into izakaya and noren-flapped tea houses. Average dinner cost per couple: 6,000–8,000 yen. Arrive before 7:30 p.m. to avoid the worst crowds.

Higashiyama, northeast of Gion, is also walkable. You'll pass Yasaka Shrine and the Philosopher’s Path, both illuminated in April. A couple of budget soba stands near Chomei Temple keep dinner under 3,000 yen.

For ryokans under 400 USD a night, consider the Kiyomizu district’s smaller family-run inns—many offer tatami and shared baths for 70,000–90,000 yen per night. You'll still be within 25 minutes of Gion on foot, but avoid the steep slope of the Kiyomizu approach if you have knee issues.

Avoid the Arashiyama mountainside; it's 45 minutes by bus from Gion, and you'll definitely need a taxi to return. The cherry blossoms there are spectacular, but the distance kills the evening vibe you want.

Practical tip: April evenings in Kyoto stay warm until 8 p.m., then cool quickly. Bring a light jacket. Most restaurants close between 10:30 and 11 p.m., so plan your walk accordingly.
